flavour.world_description: There are no animals left to sacrifice, and the rites still name their quantities. The Hekatombaia collect the difference, with immaculate procedure.
flavour.world_summary: The hunt is over and the altars are not. A hundred oxen were owed at every feast, and the hills hold none, so the debt is written in people now, correctly, in triplicate.
flavour.faction_blurb: The Hekatombaia keep the rolls. Every household owes a share of the rite, assessed by census and collected by warrant, and no clerk has ever raised their voice.
flavour.dungeon_blurb: A levy house is a granary turned counting-hall. The tallies are neat, the doors are sound, and the people inside have already been counted.
flavour.mechanic_blurb: The levy falls on the poleis that still keep the rite. Those that abandoned sacrifice have nothing to levy and nothing to bargain with, and the Hekatombaia know it.
flavour.currency_blurb: Coin is bottled vitality, and everyone at the market knows whose it was.
flavour.precedent_blurb: They cite Iphigenia at Aulis. The goddess was owed, the army was becalmed, a daughter was brought. Nobody called it a tragedy at the time. They call it a precedent.
